- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In absence of strong sentiment, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period if recent history shows downward trend.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model is overestimating, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–5 days; adjust forecast to match recent 7–14 day moving average if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model tends to hold high forecasts; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
